gmm.support: very strong support for two groups
gmm.verdict: ΔBIC = +807.0 (one group 25020.1, two groups 24213.2): very strong support for two groups. BIC compares Gaussian shapes, and a single skewed cloud can earn two components, so this is evidence, not proof. But its two groups are barely the DS / P-spike split (adjusted Rand 0.07, where 1 is the same split and 0 is chance; 63% of events the same): two Gaussians fit the cloud's SHAPE better than one, which a single skewed spectrum also does. Read the split-axis histogram before reading this as two populations.

dbic_scale: very strong support for two groups

measure.filter_label: DS filter, 5–100 Hz, 60 Hz mains out

rule: Pooled over 9 recordings from 9 mice, in pooled raw units: the cluster whose centre has more 500–1000 Hz power is called P-spike: +18.1 dB against +9.4 dB for the other, which is called DS (1640 DS, 1377 P-spike, 1 not measured; 5 resolved only with a half-width search widened past 50 ms).

scale.why: Pooled raw units, z-scored once across the pool: differences in size between mice stay visible, impedance and placement included.

split_axis.unit: z, 0 at the midpoint, DS negative
